next_step: Finalize Dedicated POC acceptance criteria + schedule infra kickoff (week of 2026-02-22)
notes:
Background: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics) building conversational assistant for support + contextual doc search for customers. Evaluated Hosted API in Jan (fast onboarding, good latency). Now moving to Dedicated POC to hit predictable throughput and data isolation requirements.

Timeline / recent activity (bulleted):
- 2026-01-13: Intro call (AE Aisha) — high level requirements: 99.9% availability target, p95 latency goal ~200ms for short chat flows, peak 150 QPS expected for backend reranking.
- 2026-01-28: Hosted API trial kickoff (ff-2026-01-28-0452). Quick results: generation quality OK, but token cost at scale a concern.
- 2026-02-03: Security call with Redwood SE (Diego) — requested SOC2 report, KMS integration options, and VPC deployment checklist.
- 2026-02-10: Pricing + roadmap call (ff-2026-02-10-1934) — discussed Dedicated reserved capacity tiers, preliminary commitment sizes (6-12 months) and discount bands.
- 2026-02-12: Internal infra spike — network engineering requested sample VPC peering diagram and expected ports.
- 2026-02-15: POC scoping workshop w/ SE + infra + product. Agreed canary + fallback routing plan, acceptance criteria draft created.

Use-case & requirements summary (shorthand):
- Workloads: conversational support assistant (context windows ~4-8k tokens), doc search + reranking for help center, scheduled summarization jobs for release notes.
- Latency / throughput targets: interactive p95 <= 200ms target for short-turn chat (non-streaming), sustained throughput 100-150 QPS for reranking flows, allow 500 QPS bursts via autoscale/burst pool.
- Cost sensitivity: unit economics matter — looking to reduce per-token cost vs hosted by 30%+ through batching + quantized variants.
- Model preferences: open models preferred (4k/8k context), willing to test quantized 4-bit variants for production if quality delta acceptable. Need model variant routing for canary and rollback.
- Routing/fallback needs: primary region usa-east, fallback to usa-west and eu-west; automatic region failover for regional outages; model variant hierarchy: full-precision -> quantized -> smaller-architect model (if capacity constrained).
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 1y, customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, data residency for EU customers.

POC plan (agreed outline):
- Scope: 2-week Dedicated POC in customer VPC with Redwood Private control plane (customer-managed VPC peering).
- Canary: start with 10% traffic to Dedicated canary (single region usa-east), 2-week canary window, monitor latency, error rates, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics on 50 prompt baseline set.
- Fallback routing: implement path-based routing policy — if canary p95 >250ms or error rate >1.5x baseline, auto-fallback to Hosted API variant in same region; if region outage, failover to secondary region (usa-west) with model variant downgrade.
- Rollback triggers: defined — quality regression above threshold (BLEU/ROUGE drop >5% on eval set), latency SLO violation p95 >250ms for >10m, or sustained error spikes. Full automated rollback + alert to on-call.
- Acceptance criteria: match or improve hosted quality on eval prompts, p95 <= 220ms for chat flows under normal load, cost per 1k tokens < target threshold (TBD), successful SAML login + KMS key rotation test.
- Deliverables: karpenter/infra diagram, runbook for canary monitoring, rollback playbook, performance dashboard + cost projection.

Pricing / commercial notes:
- Customer prefers 6 month reserved commit to start; procurement evaluating 6 vs 12 month. ARR target band ~ $60k-$120k. Pricing concession ask: deeper discount for 12-month commit + commit ladder for burst capacity.

Open items / blockers (short):
- Legal: DPA & security addendum sign-off (security team flagged data residency clause).
- Infra: VPC peering needs network CIDR approval and firewall port list from Redwood.
- Finance: budget approval for reserved commit (expected by end of Feb).
- Ops: Need SOC2 docs + penetration test summary — redwood to provide link.

Quotes / snippets: "performance looks promising but we need predictable unit cost before committing" — Head of Product (Eve Carter).

Suggested next steps (AE + SE playbook):
- Send final POC SOW with acceptance criteria and timeline (Aisha) by 2026-02-19.
- Diego to produce VPC peering diagram + ports + sample terraform snippet by 2026-02-20.
- Schedule kickoff with infra on 2026-02-24, 60-90 minute session.
- Legal: escalate DPA to contracts; aim sign-off w/in 10 business days after SOW.

Internal notes for Redwood team:
- Emphasize cost modelling in POC reporting (show per-route token costs pre/post batching).
- Prepare two model variants for canary: full-precision 8k model + quantized 4-bit 8k variant. Provide automated quality regression checks.
- Consider offering a 30-day performance credit if POC fails due to infra issues to unblock procurement.

CRM-style shorthand additions:
- Contact list: Eve Carter (Head Product) — eve.carter@spectralpine.com; Jonah Reid (Infra Lead) — jonah.reid@spectralpine.com; Maya Liu (Security) — maya.liu@spectralpine.com.
- Preferred meeting cadence: twice-weekly during POC, then biweekly post-POC.
- Notes saved to drive: drive:/notes/spectralpine-poc-logs/
short_description: Mid-market analytics SaaS evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated. Scoped 2-week Dedicated POC with canary + fallback routing (model variants, region failover, rollback). Pricing talks for reserved commit. Major blockers: VPC peering, DPA, SOC2 docs.
